chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man met another man during the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: “This man has fabricated a lie against me.” He said: “And what did he say to you?” He said: “He claimed that he had a wet dream about the other man’s mother.” He said: “Indeed, in justice, if you wish, you may flog his shadow, for a dream is only like a shadow. But we shall give him a painful beating so that he does not harm the Muslims.” So he gave him a painful beating.

key_terms.الْحُلُمَ: the dream or nocturnal vision being discussed
key_terms.الْعَدْلِ: justice in judicial assessment and proportional response
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Muslims, whose harm was to be prevented
key_terms.اِفْتَرَى: fabricated a false accusation or lie
key_terms.جَلَدْتَ: you would flog; a reference to corporal punishment
key_terms.ضَرْبًا وَجِيعًا: a painful beating as discretionary punishment
key_terms.ظِلَّهُ: his shadow; used to show the unreality of the dream

ai.seo_question: What did Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام rule about someone who insulted another person by mentioning an indecent dream?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a case brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام involving a false and offensive statement based on a dream. He clarified that no fixed hadd applies for a mere dream, comparing it to a shadow, yet he imposed a discretionary painful beating to prevent harm and abuse against Muslims. The narration reflects judicial discernment between what does and does not warrant formal legal punishment.
